Breast tuberculosis: The presence of granulomas with central caseous necrosis, epitheloid histiocytes, and Langhans' giant cells, along with the clinical presentation of a painful mass and sinus tract, are characteristic of tuberculosis.
Idiopathic granulomatous mastitis: The histopathologic findings of granulomas and lymphocytic infiltration could also be consistent with idiopathic granulomatous mastitis, although the presence of caseous necrosis and specific giant cells more strongly suggests tuberculosis.
